result:
Round 211 passes. Every C row except the root gate's ran in real Chromium or as a real harness run, at 1440×900 and 1280×720 where it matters, so `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true. The Clip Gain drag is fixed at the React level: each move now commits 3 components instead of 95. One real problem remains: while playing, a single Clip Gain drag still takes about 60 ms per move against the 16 ms target, so SABA-B-5 stays open.

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| **SCOPE-211** | Only the 14 granted files changed; the frozen-file hash check returns 0 at start and end. 2 of the 4 allowed new files appeared (A's DEVIATION 2 needs B's ruling). `budgets.json` has exactly the 12 required changes plus the 50 new members rows. The repo was unchanged by my run. |
| **PERF-RUN-211** | Both runs exit 0 (457 s and 435 s); all 92 asserts pass. The 119 rows that had to stay identical to round 210 do. `load.components` goes 344 → 345, which I confirmed in the browser is the one new Clip Gain block component. |
| **WINDOW-211** | Single and members, stopped and playing, including runs that start below max: max 3 components per move, every value-changing move commits, nothing commits before the first move. The baseline gives 95–97 on the same probe. |
| **LIVE-DISPLAY-211** | At 25/50/75 % of the drag, the number field, slider, range text and both waveforms match the baseline exactly (49 states compared, 0 differences). No pending marker mid-drag. No frame shows a snap-back on release. |
| **AUDIO-211** | The live clip gain follows the drag with 0 source starts. Sources started at a loop wrap, and the graph rebuilt by Space mid-drag, use the dragged value (single and members). Undo restores. A browser loop wrap does not rebuild the graph, so the rebuild path itself is proven by the Space restart and the CP7/CP8 tests, not by the wrap. |
| **MEMBERS-211** | With both clips audible, the 7 dB difference is kept. Cancel and blur restore both live gains, both drawings and the block, with no history entry. The clamp values match the baseline. |
| **INVARIANTS-211** | 1,523 values per viewport compared against the baseline; only random clip IDs differ. |
| **EXPORT-211** | Dragged and typed clip gain give bit-identical WAVs, for single and members. Both differ from the control exports. Run at 1440 only, since the render does not depend on viewport. |
| **VISUAL-211** | Computed styles match the baseline exactly (503 values per viewport). One 1280 crop differs by 8 pixels at a tiny anti-aliasing level. The same field is pixel-identical across builds when cropped fresh, after focus and after a forced repaint, so this is repaint noise. |
| **DOC-211, AN-REVIEW-211** | Pass. Doc 163 is corrected, which closes C-R210-01. My own two mutants each turned their tests red. |
| **G211-3** | Pass: `/studio-lab` opens with no sign-in, `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required", the token endpoint returns 401 with no header and 500 with a fake Bearer, and no token is issued. |
| **§4 adjacent items** | Pass where run: track Volume still 1 component per move, meters move, video Clip Gain disabled with its reason, waveform zoom and trim still redraw the lane. The selection change mid-drag (MG11) can't be done with one mouse, so it is covered only by the jsdom tests. |

**Findings for B:**
- **C-R211-01 (Low):** on release, before the first frame is drawn, the field briefly shows the old pre-drag value with the "Unsaved" pending state, then corrects itself. It is never painted. Strictly, it breaks D-29z189 item 7 ("when no draft exists, it shows exactly what it shows today"), and it is why the release takes 2 commits (A's DEVIATION 3).
- **C-R211-02 (SABA-B-5 remainder, recorded as a note rather than a bug):** a single Clip Gain drag while playing still measures 58–60 ms per move at p95. Stopped is about 18 ms and members while playing about 10 ms. It needs a measured follow-up in STUDIO-PERFORMANCE.
- **C-R211-03:** A's DEVIATIONS 1, 2, 4 and 5 are for B to rule on.
  - 1: the harness members scenario adds the Soft impact clip itself.
  - 2: both leaf components live inside existing files.
  - 4: timing-only harness rows moved by about 0.5 ms.
  - 5: one mutant against the setter loop does not fail any test.
- **C-R211-04:** the task assumes video lanes draw no waveform. A video clip with an audio track draws one on the baseline too, so this is not a regression.

The full suite, typecheck, build and `npm run verify` are left to the root gate and not claimed.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop`:
- c-round-211.md
- c-round-211.json
- c-round-211/ (tools, out, shots)
